findings.title: `sq stats reviews` resolves the reviews directory from the process cwd, not the git root
findings.description: `stats_reviews` builds its target as `reviews_dir = Path.cwd() / REVIEWS_DIR`, where `REVIEWS_DIR = Path("project-documents/user/reviews")` (src/squadron/review/persistence.py:32). Every other command that reads or writes artifacts under `project-documents` anchors at the git root via `resolve_repo_cwd` (src/squadron/cli/commands/review.py:292, 661; pr.py:193, 316; review_pr.py:361), and src/squadron/cli/commands/cwd_resolution.py:5-8 documents exactly why: a config `cwd` may point at a subdirectory of the repo, which "makes every repo-relative path unreadable." Running `sq stats reviews` from any subdirectory (or with such a config cwd) therefore reports `No review directory at …` and exits 0 instead of showing the report — and the command has no `--cwd` option to correct it. The tests only ever `monkeypatch.chdir` to the repo root (`tests/cli/test_stats.py::test_reviews_table_and_json`), so the subdirectory case is untested. Fix: anchor with `resolve_repo_cwd(None)` (and/or add a `--cwd` option for parity with the review commands).

findings.title: Split (multi-part) pipeline reviews lose parts 2..N spend from both stats views
findings.description: The new stamping in `ReviewAction._run_part` (src/squadron/pipeline/actions/review.py, `stamp(part.metadata, capture.record_from_review(...))`) puts a usage record on every part's `ActionResult`. But `_review` folds parts with `fold_review_parts`, whose `_metadata` keeps only `parts[0].metadata` (summing `tool_calls_made` but not the usage record), and the executor persists that single folded result in run state. Consequently `sq stats run` (src/squadron/stats/usage_report.py reads `action.metadata[USAGE_KEY]` per step) reports only part 1's spend for the step. Meanwhile every part's artifact is stamped with `runId` (traceability, slice 195 D12), so `reviews_usage_report` excludes them all into `excluded_run_ids` (src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py:88-90) and `sq stats reviews` omits their spend too. For any multi-part pipeline review — split task files are a supported flow this codebase names explicitly (`review_parts`, `name_suffix` handling) — parts 2..N spend appears in *neither* view, breaking the invariant the module docstrings state ("each review's spend appears in exactly one view"). No test asserts usage aggregation across parts (`tests/pipeline/actions/test_review_action_parts.py` doesn't touch usage). Suggested fix: aggregate the per-part `USAGE_KEY` records in `_metadata` with the same None-preserving sums as `usage_totals` (turns/tokens/cost, `priced` count), mirroring the existing `TOOL_CALLS_MADE_KEY` summation.

findings.title: Review provider-failure path logs an expected named error with a full traceback as "unexpected error"
findings.description: In the new `except ProviderError as exc:` branch of `_run_part`, after the WARNING about the saved failure artifact, the code calls `_logger.exception("review: unexpected error in step %s", context.step_name)` for a `ProviderError` — an expected, named failure whose message is already recorded. This contradicts the convention this diff itself applies in dispatch and summary ("a named provider failure (issue 200): the message says what happened, so one ERROR line and no traceback") and labels the failure "unexpected" when it is the normal provider-error path. The pre-change behavior had the same profile only via the `execute` catch-all (whose wording was also "unexpected error"); now that the branch is explicit, the traceback should be dropped (plain ERROR/WARNING) and reserved for genuinely uncaught exceptions in `execute`.

findings.title: `get_all_aliases()` re-reads both models.toml files on every model resolution and per table cell
findings.description: `_resolved` now calls `get_all_aliases()` a sixth time per resolution (`alias if alias in get_all_aliases() else None`), on top of the existing calls inside `require_known_model`, `resolve_model_alias`, `model_allows_tools`, `model_max_output_tokens`, and `model_effort` (src/squadron/models/aliases.py). Each call does `data/models.toml` + user `models.toml` `read_text()` + `tomllib.loads`; model resolution happens per step/action for every run. The new lookup could reuse a single alias-table read computed once at the top of `_resolved`. The same pattern is now also per-row in `stats_views._is_subscription` (one table lookup per cost cell rendered). Not blocking — files are small — but the per-resolution multiplication is avoidable.

findings.title: Prompt-only compact runs an LLM call but neither requires nor records a capture
findings.description: The slice's stated invariant (src/squadron/pipeline/models.py: `usage_capture` comment; `require_capture` docstring "an LLM action never runs without one") is upheld on the SDK-rotate path, but `_execute_prompt_only` dispatches `/compact` through `claude_agent_sdk.query` — a real LLM call — without ever calling `require_capture` or reading the result's usage. `COMPACT` is in `LLM_ACTION_TYPES`, so these steps surface as "N LLM action(s) have no usage recorded" in `sq stats run` (visible, not silent), but the spend is simply never captured and a missing `UsageCapture` on this path would not fail fast. Either record the compact turn's usage from the stream's result message or document the prompt-only path as an explicit exemption.

findings.title: The `api-rate equiv.` cost label is effectively unreachable in the reviews view
findings.description: `cost_cell` switches the label to "api-rate equiv." when `record.cost_basis is PROVIDER` and `_is_subscription(record.alias)` — but the standalone-review records are rebuilt from artifact frontmatter (src/squadron/stats/reviews_report.py `_record`), where `alias` is derived from `requestedModel`, which persistence only writes when the answering model *substituted* the requested one, and which holds a model id rather than an alias name (src/squadron/review/persistence.py `_review_frontmatter_lines`; review_client sets `result.requested_model = resolved_model`, a model id). So for normal runs the reviews view shows `$… prov` for subscription-alias spend while the run view shows `$… api-rate equiv.` for the same money. Either record the alias name in the artifact frontmatter or drop the subscription check from the reviews path; as written the `_is_subscription` branch is dead code for that view.

findings.title: Strong test coverage with observability assertions on the new failure paths
findings.description: The diff follows test-with conventions well: failure modes carry observable-signal tests (partial-interrupt WARNING with run/step ids in `test_stall_with_failed_drain_records_partial` and `test_partial_record_sets_flag_and_warns_with_run_and_step`; warn-once pricing in `test_pricing_warning_once_per_capture`; effort-gap log-once in `test_effort_gap_logged_once_per_capture`; "no token usage" warning-once in `tests/pipeline/test_sdk_session.py::TestSessionTelemetry::test_results_without_usage_warn_once_per_dispatch`); the JSON/table parity claim is tested both directions (`test_run_json_matches_table_rows`, `test_reviews_table_and_json`); the state round-trip is pinned (`tests/pipeline/test_state_usage.py`, including schema v3/v4/v5 pre-slice fixtures that exist on disk); and the real-CLI `ResultMessage` fixture (`tests/providers/sdk/result_fixture.py`) satisfies the project rule that parser tests use the actual production format. The missing-capture guard is tested for dispatch, summary, compact, and review.

structured_findings.summary: `sq stats reviews` resolves the reviews directory from the process cwd, not the git root
Split (multi-part) pipeline reviews lose parts 2..N spend from both stats views
Review provider-failure path logs an expected named error with a full traceback as "unexpected error"
`get_all_aliases()` re-reads both models.toml files on every model resolution and per table cell
Prompt-only compact runs an LLM call but neither requires nor records a capture
The `api-rate equiv.` cost label is effectively unreachable in the reviews view
Strong test coverage with observability assertions on the new failure paths
